domain: Political Linguistics / State Formation / Commitment Systems
topic_summary: Analysis of Turkey's 1928 alphabet reform (Law 1353), which replaced Arabic script with Latin script within months via top-down imposition. The reform had effectively zero prior practitioners of Latin-script Turkish, making it the cleanest test case for whether a commitment system kernel can be installed without prior occupancy of the new reading—a potential M-set gap scenario where authority creates interpretive space ex nihilo rather than selecting among existing readings.

key_entities: Mustafa Kemal Atatürk (state founder; reform architect)
Turkish Grand National Assembly (legislative body enacting Law 1353)
Ottoman Arabic script (pre-reform writing system; 600+ year tradition)
Latin alphabet (imposed replacement system; zero prior Turkish practitioners)
Turkish Language Association (post-reform authority body, est. 1932)
Literate Ottoman elite (pre-reform reading class rendered functionally illiterate)
key_tensions: State modernization imperative vs cultural-religious continuity (Kemalist state vs Ottoman tradition)
Linguistic accessibility (phonetic Latin fit) vs historical archive access (Arabic script corpus)
Authority legitimacy grounding: revolutionary mandate vs textual continuity (new state vs Ottoman legitimacy)

commitment_system_recognition.kernel_description: The graphemic substrate of Turkish linguistic identity—what writing system encodes legitimate Turkish and who can read/write it
commitment_system_recognition.authority_description: State monopoly on literacy instruction and orthographic standardization, grounded in revolutionary founding rather than textual tradition
commitment_system_recognition.kernel_collapse_reason: This is NOT a contested kernel. There was no prior Latin-script reading to contest with Arabic-script reading—the 'contest' is between having a kernel (Arabic script as legitimacy substrate) and destroying it to install a new one. The structural question is whether kernel installation without prior reading occupancy is possible, not which of multiple readings interprets a shared commitment. The Arabic and Latin scripts do not read the same kernel differently—they ARE different kernels for different state formations. This is kernel replacement, not kernel contestation.
commitment_system_recognition.structural_reframing: The topic decomposes into three axes: (1) the mountain of phonetic mismatch between Arabic script and Turkish phonology, (2) the tangled_rope of archive severance as deliberate elite displacement, and (3) the scaffold of revolutionary authority attempting to install legitimacy without textual grounding. The M-set gap is not about readings but about whether a commitment system can function when the kernel has no prior interpretive community.

omegas.description: The topic was flagged as contested kernel but collapses under §1.3-K analysis. Arabic and Latin scripts are not two readings of one kernel—they are two different kernels for two different state formations (Ottoman vs Kemalist). The structural question is kernel replacement feasibility, not reading contestation. This is a category error in the initial framing, now corrected.

Does revolutionary_legitimacy_scaffold succeed as a commitment system with zero prior reading community? If the M-set (interpretive community) is empty at kernel installation, can the authority create legitimacy ex nihilo, or does the system collapse into pure coercion without commitment structure? The 1928 reform's durability (95+ years) suggests success, but the mechanism remains uncertain—was it scaffold → rope transition via generational replacement, or did it remain scaffold indefinitely?
omegas.source: §2.2 Dark Matter Probe 2 (Absence Inventory) + revolutionary_legitimacy_scaffold analysis

omegas.description: Is archive_severance_mechanism a one-way ratchet or reversible via re-education? Post-1980s Ottoman script instruction in universities suggests partial reversibility, but the generational gap (1928-1980s) may have created irreversible institutional knowledge loss. If reversible, the tangled_rope classification holds; if irreversible, it may be a snare with permanent victim set expansion.
omegas.source: §2.2 Dark Matter Probe 3 (Beneficiary Scan) + archive_severance_mechanism classification uncertainty

omegas.description: Is phonetic_script_mismatch a true mountain (Arabic script fundamentally unsuited to Turkish phonology) or a piton of Ottoman scribal practice (solvable via diacritic standardization)? Ottoman Turkish had developed some vowel notation conventions; the reform may have been politically motivated rather than linguistically necessary. If piton, the entire downstream structure reclassifies.

How does Turkish reform compare to other top-down script changes (Mongolian Cyrillic 1941, Kazakh Latin 2017-2031, Azerbaijani Latin 1991)? Do they exhibit similar M-set gaps, or did they have prior reading communities? Comparative analysis may reveal whether zero-occupancy kernel installation is unique to Turkish or a general pattern.
omegas.source: §2.2 Dark Matter Probe 1 (Operational Medium) + domain boundary question
